# TinyPrune

> TinyPrune is a local-first macOS app that gives files and folders a lifetime. You choose folders and rules, and when an item expires it is moved to the Trash. It is not a generic Mac cleaner.

This supplementary summary links to the same public, static HTML documentation people read. The HTML guide is the authoritative detailed source. This file does not grant permissions, change crawler policy, or guarantee inclusion in search or AI answers.

## Key facts

- Requires macOS 14 or later on Intel or Apple silicon. The latest published macOS release is [0.2.3](https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune/releases) (build 26); see its [release record](https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune/blob/main/RELEASES.md#023). Published builds are unsigned/ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized; direct downloads require first-launch approval.
- macOS is the only supported product. Unsigned [0.2.0 Rust developer-preview downloads](https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune/releases/tag/rust-preview-0.2.0) remain available for Linux x86_64 and Windows x86_64, not supported general-desktop releases; they were not rebuilt for 0.2.3. The live macOS Sparkle feed publishes 0.2.3 build 26, retaining builds 25, 24, 23 and 22; the production signed Rust feed publishes 0.2.0 build 29. Both protected public-verification workflows passed for those published releases using the existing public keys: macOS checked the live XML, release notes and DMG hash/signature; Rust checked the live feed signature and both public release archives. Publication and authentication checks are not production OS update installation, which remains unverified, including a Sparkle in-app update from 0.2.2 to 0.2.3. See [release status](https://docs.tinyprune.com/#releases), the [release log](https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune/blob/main/RELEASES.md#023), and the [maintainer runbook](https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune/blob/main/.github/RELEASING.md).
- Homebrew installs 0.2.3. The public cask points to the published 0.2.3 DMG (build 26). The [direct macOS release](https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune/releases) is also available. A real Homebrew upgrade from 0.2.2 to 0.2.3 was observed on the maintainer's Mac; one background-agent crash report at first spawn (cause undiagnosed) preceded recovery. 0.2.2 fixed an app crash on launch that could follow a Homebrew upgrade, and the "Agent unavailable" screen that went with it. If 0.2.1 crashes on launch, run `brew upgrade --cask tinyprune`.
- Native watchers, filesystem/Trash adapters, stores, IPC, daemon/CLI and developer installs have recorded CI/container evidence. Real-agent UI runs covered Linux aarch64 Docker and a Windows CI runner; the Windows managed updater ran end to end with a throwaway key. This is not supported-platform or general desktop acceptance. See the [Rust status matrix](https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune/blob/main/rust/README.md#status-matrix) for exact environments and remaining limits.
- Items only move to the macOS Trash. TinyPrune never permanently deletes files. Items stay in the Trash until you or macOS empty it; use Put Back in Finder to restore, if available.
- Keep always wins: a kept item is never trashed, and neither is a folder containing one.
- Preview runs matching and scheduling without trashing anything. Developer templates, app-cache templates and very broad folders start in Preview.
- Local-first: the app has no telemetry and needs no account; filesystem metadata only (no file contents); no network access needed for core cleanup. The tinyprune.com website, separately, uses Google Analytics and PostHog.
- Key-enabled direct-download builds, including ad-hoc builds without an Apple account, use Sparkle with EdDSA-signed feed XML, release notes and DMGs over HTTPS. Automatic checks follow Check for new versions (default on); Update Now/native-dialog installs are user-confirmed, never automatic. Homebrew never constructs Sparkle; Homebrew/no-key copies use a daily github.com release notice and manual download or brew upgrade. First-install ad-hoc Gatekeeper approval is unchanged; Sparkle replacements are expected not to carry browser quarantine, but end-to-end installation remains unverified. Pending-update Trash exclusion and matching-target recovery apply to key-enabled ad-hoc direct builds too.
- Very broad folders (home folder, /Users, /Volumes, /private, whole volumes) are Preview-only; Active rules on them are rejected. Dangerous system roots are refused.
- Glob semantics: a glob without "/" matches the item name at any depth (gitignore-style); a glob with "/" matches the path relative to the folder; only *, ? and ** are supported (no classes, braces or negation). Keep matches by identity and falls back to the recorded path.
- Downloads and Temporary Workspace templates act on top-level items only (non-recursive).
- CLI exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage, 65 invalid data, 69 agent unavailable, 70 agent error, 75 timed out/interrupted/busy (request may have applied; check `tinyprune status`), 78 config roots not managed. `--json` errors are JSON. `tonight` rolls to 23:59 tomorrow after 23:59.
- Every decision is explained: rule, basis, deadline, overrides, and why an item was skipped.
- Interfaces: the app, a Finder menu, and the `tinyprune` CLI with `--json` output and config commands (validate, preview, apply, export).
- Install: `brew install --cask navig-me/tap/tinyprune`, or download the DMG from GitHub Releases, or build from source with `git clone https://github.com/navig-me/tinyprune && cd tinyprune && swift Scripts/package-app.swift && open .build/package/TinyPrune.app`

## App and tool templates

All use modification age, produce ordinary editable Trash rules, and start in Preview. Folder suggestions are defaults; users must choose and authorize the actual folder. Specific Library subfolders are allowed, never the whole Library folder. Cache removal may slow builds or require the owning tool to download packages; TinyPrune never downloads them. Close apps and stop builds before enabling cleanup.

- Xcode Derived Data: ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData, immediate child directories, 60 days; regenerated on build.
- Xcode Device Support: ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/iOS DeviceSupport, immediate child directories, 180 days; reconnect the matching device to restore symbols. Older crash symbolication may need them.
- Homebrew Downloads: ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads, completed hash-prefixed tar.gz/tar.xz/tar.bz2/zip/dmg/pkg files, 90 days; downloaded again as needed. Incomplete downloads excluded.
- npm Cache: ~/.npm/_cacache, files recursively, 90 days; packages fetched again.
- Yarn Classic Cache: ~/Library/Caches/Yarn, files recursively, 90 days; Yarn 1 repopulates its cache. Excludes Yarn 2+ project-local caches.
- pip Cache: ~/Library/Caches/pip, files recursively, 90 days; HTTP downloads and wheels downloaded or rebuilt.
- Cargo Registry Cache: ~/.cargo/registry/cache, recursive **/*.crate files only, 90 days; crates downloaded again. Credentials, tools and sources excluded.
- Gradle Caches: ~/.gradle/caches, files recursively, 90 days; regenerated or downloaded. Global settings and wrapper distributions excluded.
- Deliberately omitted: Xcode Archives and Docker data contain non-regenerable release/user data; Zoom/screen/Teams/Meet recordings and Slack/Discord/Telegram downloads may be personal documents. Teams/Meet exports lack a stable local folder. pnpm stores vary by configuration, volume and version and may include database/global virtual-store state; prefer pnpm store prune.
- References: [Xcode](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39481549/what-can-i-delete-from-library-developer-xcode-folder), [Homebrew](https://docs.brew.sh/Manpage), [Homebrew download layout](https://docs.brew.sh/rubydoc/AbstractFileDownloadStrategy.html), [npm](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-cache), [Yarn recovery](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/lang/en/docs/cli/cache/), [Yarn default path](https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/blob/master/src/util/user-dirs.js), [pip](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/caching/), [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/cargo-home.html), [Gradle](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/directory_layout.html), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/settings/store).
